thought.text: No `curl`/`wget` in the base image, but I can install `curl` from the working Debian repos first. Now let me patch the Dockerfile:

reasoning_content:
The base image doesn't have `curl` or `wget`, but it does have `sha256sum` and `apt-get`. So within the Dockerfile, either of the following is possible:
1. Install `ca-certificates` + `curl` from the working Debian repositories, then use that to download the .deb files.
2. Alternatively, there's a method to disable the broken pgdg.list, install curl, and then install the .deb files.

Let me rewrite the RUN step of the Dockerfile:

```dockerfile
FROM postgis/postgis:17-3.5

# Update package lists and install pgRouting for PostgreSQL 17
# The upstream PGDG repository no longer provides packages for bullseye (EOL),
# so install pgrouting from the .deb on the PostgreSQL APT archive with a verified checksum.
RUN rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pgdg.list && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts.deb \
        "https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_all.deb" && \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting.deb \
        "https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_amd64.deb" && \
    echo "594cbaca6af23694486ef46f7ec23c49061444562eb0ab2a13bb169bcb6259fa  /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts.deb" | sha256sum -c - && \
    echo "cbbec04156828a4d9eb11a73560b49c8312a46b30534053608d272329af27ee2  /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting.deb" | sha256sum -c - && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting.deb && \
    rm -f /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting*.deb
```

Wait a sec — one question: does apt-get install on a .deb resolve dependencies? No, apt install <file> will (on modern apt) automatically install missing dependencies from the configured repositories. The pgrouting deb depends on `postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts (>= 3.8.0)`, `postgresql-17`, `postgresql-17-postgis`, `postgresql-17-postgis-scripts` — all already installed in the base image (postgresql-17, postgresql-17-postgis-3, postgresql-17-postgis-3-scripts). Only the scripts deb is missing, but I'm installing both explicitly, so no problem.

Wait a sec: does `postgresql-17` exist as a separately installed package? dpkg -l showed `postgresql-17` as already installed (ii). Good. And `postgresql-17-postgis` — is this a virtual package provided by postgresql-17-postgis-3? Yes, postgresql-17-postgis-3 provides postgresql-17-postgis. No problem.

Note that the `+1` in the URL `3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1` should be fine in the shell (it's not a glob character… the `+` is literal, so OK). The quotes also protect it.

Another thing to consider: `apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends /tmp/...deb` — if there are unmet dependencies, will apt automatically attempt to fix them? In the case of a local .deb, `apt-get install ./file.deb` resolves dependencies from the repositories. But the only configured repositories are the working debian.org ones (I removed pgdg.list), and curl/ca-certificates come from there. The dependencies on postgresql-17, etc. are already installed, so no downloads are needed. Good.

Alright, let me write the new Dockerfile. I'll keep the changes minimal and focused.

Also, I should double-check whether there are any other places in the repository that reference the postgres Dockerfile or the pgrouting apt repository. The docker-compose.prod.yml also builds from ./postgres with the same Dockerfile, so fixing the single Dockerfile covers both dev and prod.

Now, let me apply the patch.

action.command:
cat > /workspace/deployment/postgres/Dockerfile <<'EOF'
FROM postgis/postgis:17-3.5

# Update package lists and install pgRouting for PostgreSQL 17.
# The upstream PGDG apt repository no longer publishes the bullseye (EOL)
# suite, so pgrouting is installed from its published .deb files on the
# PostgreSQL APT archive, verified against the SHA256 sums published in the
# archive's Packages index.
RUN rm -f /etc/apt/sources.list.d/pgdg.list && \
    apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/* && \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts.deb \
        "https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_all.deb" && \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting.deb \
        "https://apt-archive.postgresql.org/pub/repos/apt/pool/main/p/pgrouting/postgresql-17-pgrouting_3.8.0-1.pgdg110+1_amd64.deb" && \
    echo "594cbaca6af23694486ef46f7ec23c49061444562eb0ab2a13bb169bcb6259fa  /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting-scripts.deb" | sha256sum -c - && \
    echo "cbbec04156828a4d9eb11a73560b49c8312a46b30534053608d272329af27ee2  /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting.deb" | sha256sum -c - && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting.deb && \
    rm -f /tmp/postgresql-17-pgrouting*.deb && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
EOF
cd /workspace/deployment && docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml build db 2>&1 | tail -25
